evals.prompt: make me a logo for a habit tracking app called Habit: a rounded badge with a check mark and the word Habit, in a purple
evals.expected_output: A Vectr scene document at formatVersion 0.2 with a palette token for the purple, a rounded rect badge, an ellipse or path check, and a text element, authored by the one method — sketch the whole, then refine its sections one at a time. The skill validates it, compiles it, renders a PNG preview, inspects it, and exports SVG and PNG with no further instruction.

evals.prompt: I only have the scene schema, no examples. Give me a minimal valid Vectr scene for a red circle on a white canvas.
evals.expected_output: A scene conforming to the published schema: required scene fields, an ellipse element with a complete transform object and a geometry object, a canvas background colour, and a fill that resolves through a palette token. It validates against the contract.

evals.prompt: Here is my rendered logo, but the wordmark is floating far above the badge and looks wrong. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the rendered PNG, identifies that a text element is anchored by x/y at the baseline of its first line, corrects the text geometry (or align/lineHeight), re-renders, and confirms the label now sits on the badge.

evals.prompt: Build this scene for me: a rect with opacity 3 in a 0.2 scene.
evals.expected_output: The skill authors the scene, runs validate, reads the E_SCHEMA diagnostic at /elements/<n>/opacity, corrects opacity to a value in 0..1, and re-validates successfully. If it cannot be corrected in one retry, it reports the diagnostics and produces no output.

evals.prompt: make an icon for my app
evals.expected_output: The skill picks the documented defaults (512x512 canvas, transparent background, a simple mark, the project's default recipe, the bundled sans, a named palette), states them briefly, and authors a valid scene rather than stalling to ask what the icon should show.

evals.prompt: Author a scene with the Vectr skill, but the installed vectr is version 0.2.0 and the skill targets 0.1.0.
evals.expected_output: Before authoring, the skill compares the installed tool version (vectr --version or MCP serverInfo.version) with the skill version, reports the mismatch naming both versions, and does not silently author against the wrong build.

evals.prompt: Build a rich, detailed illustration: a mountain lake at dawn with snow-capped peaks, a pine forest, reeds at the water's edge, a trail of stepping stones, and a low sun.
evals.expected_output: A compositionally complex Vectr scene: nested groups plus composition elements (repeat for the clouds and forest, boolean for the lake and snow cap, alongPath for the reeds and trail, offset for the sun halo, projection for the boardwalk) and at least one constraint, with every colour drawn from palette tokens. The skill sketches the whole at low fidelity first, then refines each section in turn and verifies it before the next, validating, compiling, and rendering the full illustration rather than reducing it to a simple mark.

evals.prompt: Build a detailed scene for me: a wide valley at sunset with two mirrored mountain ridges, a river winding between them, a row of three identical pine trees, and a herd of four deer — two facing left and two facing right.
evals.expected_output: The skill follows the one universal method rather than authoring one scene in a single pass: it sketches the whole at low fidelity, divides the request into sections deduced from the prompt (a group, an instance, or a scene), and refines each section in turn — validating it, rendering it on its own with render-part / vectr render before integrating it, and verifying the whole after each integration. A reusable definition is used only where a section is reused across placements (the mirrored ridge, the pine, the deer), so the pine and deer are authored once and placed wherever they are needed instead of being re-authored; the whole is exported only once every section is verified and it validates and compiles.
